finding: The original TLS ClientHello prewarming mechanism; this is not a modern end-to-end zero-latency guarantee.
The later design explicitly discusses cold starts, sparse traffic, isolate eviction and sharding.
Use the actual deployment build for local startup profiling; local CPU durations are not deployed startup latency.
Production CPU capture samples a loaded isolate; the captured production profile here was idle and cannot exclude startup CPU.
Separate edge and backend Workers where backend round trips justify placement. Placement was tested rather than removed on assumption.
Lazy module loading requires preserving separate modules; a dynamic import bundled into the entrypoint is insufficient.
Separate cumulative curl DNS/TCP/TLS timing from post-TLS first-byte waiting.
